messages:
ashley: Quick experiment update — trying to align the continuous-batcher window with partial-decode checkpoints to reduce streaming stalls. TL;DR: p95 latency down ~8% in traces, throughput roughly flat, but KV-cache hit rate dipped ~1.5%. Details below.

liam: Can you paste the exact config you changed? also what workload (prompt lengths / toks) did you run?

ashley: Sure — synthetic chat mix, mean prompt 48 tokens, response target ~256 tokens. Local perf runner with #streams=500, concurrency 200. Config snippet: 
```
batching:
  window_ms: 10
  min_tokens: 1
  token_budget: 1024
  max_batch_size: 64
streaming:
  flush_on_partial_decode: true
  partial_decode_stride: 32
  partial_decode_timeout_ms: 6
queue_policy:
  prioritize_latency: true
  max_queue_depth: 2048
```

ashley: Notes: previously window_ms=20 and partial_decode_stride=64. New smaller window makes batches form faster which reduces wait time for first token emit, and we schedule partial-decode at stride boundaries to avoid re-decoding thoughts.

zhang: Interesting. Did you profile kernel handoff overhead? smaller window means more frequent kernel selections and possibly more kernel switching cost (especially when we toggle between fp16 and int8 paths).

ashley: Yes — I captured trace spans. Kernel-selection overhead per request increased ~0.9ms on average, but saved ~9ms wait time from batching. Net win on p95.

liam: What about KV cache behavior? you said hit rate dropped. Is that due to more fragmented batches causing more KV cache evictions or because partial-decode scheduling touches cache differently?

ashley: Good question. The drop seems correlated with increased interleaving of short and long sequences in a batch: short sequences were getting pushed through int8 fast-path while long ones stayed on fp16, so shared KV segments were less coalesced. KV hit rate dropped from 92.4% -> 90.9% in the lab run. Evidence in trace: repeated kvcache-miss spikes aligned with kernel-routing decisions.

zhang: So maybe we should bias batch formation to group by kernel-compatibility tag (quantization class) as an additional soft key. e.g., batch_key = (model_version, quant_class, stream_length_bucket). That keeps KV locality and reduces kernel switches.

ashley: I tried a simple soft grouping: allow up to 3 windows to accumulate before forcing cross-quant merge. Result: p95 slightly worse (back to -4% vs baseline), KV hit recovered to 91.8%. Tradeoff is interesting.

taylor: Another lever: adaptive window that shrinks when active_streams < 300 and expands when > 1000. Also tie token_budget to active_streams (e.g., token_budget = base * sqrt(active_streams)). That could stabilize both latency and KV locality.

liam: +1 to adaptive. Also add a short-grace for streams that previously saw high cache hits — keep them sticky for N batches. Sticky affinity to reduce eviction churn.

runtime-ci: Bench CI: ran cluster canary with window_ms=10 + partial_decode_stride=32 on cluster-24 (1k virtual clients). Results: baseline p95=125ms, candidate p95=115ms, mean tokens/sec +1.8%, KV hit rate -1.3%. CPU usage on host GPUs up ~2%. Full logs: /ci/artifacts/1787654321/trace.tar.gz

bench-bot: Canary observed transient spike at 1787654350: queue-depth climbed to 3.2k for ~7s, correlated with a 1.6x burst of short prompts from the synthetic generator. Reaction: :warning: consider applying burst-protection fallback to increase window_ms temporarily.

ashley: Noted. Plan: run A/B where group A uses adaptive-window + kernel-grouping + sticky-affinity; group B uses fixed small window but kernel override to force quant-class homogeneity per batch. Will run 24h overnight and share dashboards. Will also try lowering partial_decode_timeout_ms from 6->3 to see if that reduces KV touch frequency.

liam: Can you tag an experiment id and create a perf dashboard link? also include a config diff for rollout.

ashley: Experiment id: exp/stream-batch-20260214-01. Dashboard: https://redwood-internal/dashboards/exp-stream-batch-20260214-01. Config diff will be in the PR and I pushed a prototype branch: github.com/redwood/inference/compare/ashley/stream-batch-tune. cc @zhang @taylor :thinking:

zhang: Thanks — if the adaptive policy works we should fold it into autoscaler heuristics to avoid manual knobs. Also add a kernel-selection counter to per-route telemetry so we can alert on hot flips.

ashley: Will do. I'll post summary and metrics after the 24h run. :thumbsup:
